title: Stability campaigns canvas and team commitments
content:
Executive summary:

This doc proposes a campaign-oriented approach to operationalizing service stability and SLOs across product, platform, and customer-facing teams. Instead of one monolithic rollout, we run 3-month 'stability campaigns' focused on discrete groups of services. Each campaign uses a concise canvas to align objectives, hypotheses, metrics, and team commitments.

Why campaigns?
- Concentrated focus: smaller scope helps deliver measurable wins quickly.
- Clear ownership: one campaign lead + a compact cross-functional pod reduces coordination friction.
- Experimentation-friendly: try different error-budget policies, canary tactics, and alert thresholds without company-wide risk.

Campaign Canvas (one page) — fields to capture at kickoff:
1) Campaign name and service cluster: e.g., "Textgen-frontend stability campaign"
2) Sponsor & lead: product sponsor, SRE lead, engineering owner
3) Objective (SMART): e.g., reduce p99 latency tail from 1.6s to 1.0s for gen endpoints within 8 weeks
4) Hypothesis: technical and behavioral (e.g., "Autoscaling config + reduced cold-starts will lower p99; team will accept 2% traffic steering for canary")
5) Primary SLO(s) and target windows: latency SLO 99th < 1.0s over 30d; availability SLO 99.95% monthly
6) Success metrics / evaluation plan: list of metrics, dashboards, and pass/fail gating criteria
7) Experiment matrix: changes to try (autoscaler params, batching settings, cache TTL tweaks, model-variant fallbacks) and expected impact
8) Risks and rollback criteria: e.g., increased 50x request fanout risk; automatic cutoff if error-rate delta > 0.2%
9) Communication plan: release notes, runbook updates, customer comms if SLA-impacting
10) Deliverables and timeline: milestones and owners

Example SLO tiers and policy flavors (campaigns can select one):
- Guardrail SLO: strict uptime (99.99%) with automatic fallback to older model build on degradation
- Business SLO: broader availability target (99.9%) with manual escalation path
- Product SLO: UX-oriented metric (median latency < 200ms) used by product to gauge end-user experience

Cross-functional roles and commitments
- Campaign lead (SRE): drive the canvas, schedule checkpoints, own dashboards and canary plumbing
- Engineering owner: implement code-level changes, feature flags, and rollout hooks
- Product sponsor: prioritize backlog and approve acceptable UX tradeoffs
- Observability engineer: ensure metric coverage, tracing, and synthetic checks exist before experiments
- Support & Success: prepare customer-facing FAQ and incident templates

Two-week sprint map (6 sprints = 12 weeks campaign) — lightweight cadence
Sprint 0 (pre-campaign, 1 week): validate metrics, synthetic checks, smoke dashboards, test harness for canaries
Sprint 1: baseline analysis, quick wins (tune autoscaler thresholds, add caching for cold paths)
Sprint 2: implement controlled canary routing + feature flags; run traffic-steering experiment (1% -> 5%)
Sprint 3: measure, iterate on model variant fallback and batch sizing; rollback criteria exercise
Sprint 4: resilience hardening (timeout budgets, circuit-breaker tuning), run load soak test at 2x usual traffic
Sprint 5: SLO assessment, finalize runbooks, training session for on-call rotation
Sprint 6 (wrap): retro, artifacts handoff to maintenance, decide next campaign or scale-up

Measurement plan and tooling checklist (must be green before production experiments)
- Metric parity: same SLO metrics in dashboards and alerting backends
- Synthetic coverage: 3–5 synthetic checks that exercise critical paths
- Tracing: end-to-end traces for p95/p99 slow requests; correlate to infra signals (GPU/CPU, queue depth)
- Canary plumbing: stable traffic-splitting, auto rollback hooks, and test traffic generator
- Alert burn-down board: track noisy alerts and suppress before campaign goes live

Incident handling & escalation (lightweight)
- First responder: engineering owner on-call for the service cluster
- SRE lead: responsible for incident coordination and policy-based fallbacks
- Product & Support: notify only for customer-impacting degradation after initial triage
- Runbook snippets to include: quick rollback command, temporary rate-limit commands, where to flip golden-model routing

Communication and enablement
- Weekly sync (30 mins): campaign lead, eng owner, observability, product sponsor, support rep
- Asynchronous status: campaign heartbeat doc updated twice weekly with: progress, metric snapshot, next steps, blockers
- Education: 1-hour workshop mid-campaign on "SLO thinking for engineers" with hands-on exercises using the campaign's metrics

Gating & launch checklist (must pass all green items)
- SLO dashboards in staging and prod match (names, units, aggregation windows)
- Synthetic checks passing at 5x baseline load for 10 minutes
- Canary rollback validated in staging and rehearsed once in prod dry-run
- Alert noise reduced to <3 actionable alerts per on-call shift for the campaign's service

Hand-off and long-term maintenance
- After campaign wrap, maintainers receive a one-page runbook and a 3-month monitoring watchbook (what to watch, who to call)
- Prioritized backlog items (observability debt, infra changes) created and linked to product roadmap

Risk register (top items and mitigations)
- Risk: Model-fallback increases latency unexpectedly. Mitigation: do fallback behind a rate-limited gate and run A/B measurement before full steer.
- Risk: Alert fatigue spikes. Mitigation: temporary suppression windows and a rapid alert triage session.
- Risk: Resource overcommit leading to cross-tenant interference. Mitigation: quota guard and scheduled capacity bump for soak tests.

Quick artifacts to produce for each campaign (deliverables)
- Campaign canvas (this doc) — single page
- Synthetic check matrix (list + owners)
- Canary runbook + rollback checklist
- Post-campaign report (metrics vs. hypothesis, decisions, next steps)

Suggested OKRs for Stability Campaign program (quarterly)
- Objective: Improve customer-facing latency and availability for high-traffic endpoints
  - KR1: Run 4 stability campaigns covering top-10 services by traffic
  - KR2: Reduce average p99 latency across targeted endpoints by 20% quarter-over-quarter
  - KR3: Achieve post-campaign hand-off with runbooks for 90% of campaigns

Open questions for the steering group (to resolve before first campaign)
1) Allocation of SRE time per campaign (T-shirt sizing: small=0.25 FTE, medium=0.5 FTE, large=1.0 FTE)
2) Priority ordering mechanism if two campaigns compete for the same infra resources
3) Thresholds for automated vs. manual rollbacks and who signs off on them

Immediate next steps (owner assignments)
- Mariana Lopez (SRE): finalize campaign canvas template and create a template doc in Drive (due 2024-11-12)
- Ethan Park (observability): validate synthetic checks and deploy one test check by 2024-11-19
- Rina Gupta (engineering): identify first service cluster and provide baseline metrics by 2024-11-19
- Samuel Ortiz (product): confirm sponsor and acceptance criteria by 2024-11-15

Appendix: short checklist for on-call rotations during campaigns
- On-call buddy: rotate an additional buddy for the campaign window (for 2-week sprints)
- Post-incident note: every incident during campaign requires a 24-hour note in the campaign heartbeat doc
- Blameless capture: keep all notes in a dedicated campaign thread and summarize in post-campaign report

End of doc.
